report.summary: Chunk 11 of worktree.py: reap logic, _forget_allocation, _report_unverifiable_records, _refs_containing, _delete_unused_branch (declaration only).
risks: _refs_containing | medium | The docstring mentions a mutation that SURVIVED the suite until 2026-07-28 and is killed now by test_reap_retains_a_branch_when_git_cannot_say_who_contains_its_tip. This is a historical note; current code appears safe but the risk is that similar issues might exist elsewhere. | Check if the mentioned test exists and passes, and review git history for the mutation.

symbols.name: _forget_allocation
symbols.note: Removes allocation from self._allocations and calls _discard_allocation.

symbols.name: _report_unverifiable_records
symbols.note: Returns list of on-disk records not in current allocations, with action 'unverifiable'.

symbols.name: _refs_containing
symbols.note: Returns list of refs (excluding given branch) that contain the given SHA. Returns empty list on git failure.

symbols.name: _delete_unused_branch
symbols.note: Declaration only; body not in this chunk.

claims.text: the worktree is still in use
claims.why: This is a reason string; the condition that triggers it is not in this chunk.

claims.text: branch tip {tip} is not the allocation tip {expected}: it holds commits this manager did not create, and deleting it would destroy work
claims.why: The logic that produces this reason is present (tip != expected), but the claim about destroying work is a justification that is not checked here.

claims.text: no other ref contains {tip}, so deleting {branch} would orphan it and the commits behind it
claims.why: The code checks if holders is empty and appends this reason; the claim matches the code.

claims.text: tip is unchanged since allocation and is still reachable from {holders[0]}; no work is lost
claims.why: The code sets this reason after successful deletion; the claim matches the logic.

claims.text: This manager did not allocate it in this process; an allocation record on disk is candidate-writable and is not evidence of anything
claims.why: The function returns rows with that exact reason text.

claims.text: Reported rather than ignored so the leak is visible; reported WITHOUT any field parsed out of the file, because every byte in it is candidate-writable and echoing a forged branch name back at an operator as though it meant something is how the previous version printed false reasons.
claims.why: The function sets branch and path to None, and record to file name, not parsing content. The claim is accurate.

claims.text: The one input to the reap decision that no candidate can forge. If this is non-empty, deleting the branch cannot orphan a commit -- every commit on it stays reachable from something else. If it is empty the branch is the only thing holding that history, and holding history is exactly what this method must never destroy.
claims.why: The function returns holders list; if empty, branch is retained (see reap_branches logic). The claim is consistent.

claims.text: A FAILED CALL IS NOT AN ANSWER. git being missing, the repository being locked, .git being written by something else, a candidate that exhausted the handle table -- none of those is evidence that the tip is held elsewhere, so none of them may license a delete. Deleting the except below lets the RuntimeError escape reap_branches instead of retaining; that mutation SURVIVED the suite until 2026-07-28, and it is killed now by test_reap_retains_a_branch_when_git_cannot_say_who_contains_its_tip.
claims.why: The code catches RuntimeError and returns empty list, retaining the branch. The claim about the test is uncheckable (test not in chunk), but the behavior matches.

claims.text: Compared case-INSENSITIVELY although git refs are case-sensitive: the only effect of a spurious match is that a ref is dropped from the holder list, which retains the branch. Erring toward retention is the correct direction for a method whose failure mode is deleting work.
claims.why: The code uses casefold() for comparison, as described. The reasoning is present.

observations.what: The function _refs_containing returns empty list on git failure, which retains the branch. This is consistent with fail-closed design.
The docstring of _refs_containing references a historical bug and a test name that is not in this chunk.
The reason strings in reap_branches are informative but not checked for correctness beyond the condition that triggers them.
